title: Shell tab completion (zsh + bash) for beads-utils scripts
description: Add CLI tab completion for the repo's scripts. Dynamic value completion where it helps (bead ids for bd-view, session uuids/titles for claude-session-report), directory completion for the project-path scripts, and --flag completion for all. Support both zsh and bash. No caching in v1, but architect the candidate-enumeration as a single chokepoint so a TTL cache can be added shortly after.
notes:
DESIGN (approved):
- Single front-door helper script 'bd-complete' (Python, repo conventions) is the only thing the shell completion files call. Subcommands: 'ids' (bd list --status=all --limit 0 --json -> shortid<TAB>title) and 'sessions' (uuid<TAB>title). This is the SINGLE chokepoint where a TTL cache will be added later; no call sites change when caching lands.
- claude-session-report gains a real (non-hidden) --list-sessions flag: prints uuid<TAB>title for every known session, reusing session_titles() + a new factored iter_sessions() generator (resolve_session refactored to share it -> DRY within the script). bd-complete sessions shells out to this so session-enumeration logic stays in its home script and is never duplicated.
- completions/beads-utils.zsh + completions/beads-utils.bash are pure glue: compdef/complete wiring + per-command flag lists (transcribed from argparse) only. Zero enumeration logic in shell -> no cross-shell duplication.
- Completion map: bd-view->bead ids (short form, title as zsh desc); claude-session-report->sessions; bd-log/bd-export-csv/bd-dolt-check->dir completion for positional + own flags; claude-session-find->flags only.
- Install: source one file per shell from rc (most standard/least-surprising/no compinit-ordering footgun). README also notes fpath/bash-completion.d alternative.
- No caching in v1 (user expects to add it shortly).
- Shells: zsh + bash.
close_reason: Added zsh+bash tab completion via single bd-complete front door; verified by user in a live oh-my-zsh shell (full ids + titles, sessions, flags, dir completion; no _bd-* function leak).

title: CI polish: Node 24 actions, drop unused cache, badge, smoke test, harden discovery
description: Follow-ups after the first lint CI run (beads-utils-v9o.3) went green with 2 warnings. (1) Node 20 deprecation: bump actions/checkout@v4->v5 and astral-sh/setup-uv@v6->v8 (Node 24; GitHub forces it 2026-06-02). (2) Cache warning: add enable-cache:false to setup-uv (no lock files to key a cache on). (3) Add an Actions status badge to README. (4) Add a smoke-test step that runs each script's --version so argparse breakage (invisible to ruff) fails CI. (5) Harden shebang discovery with a guard so an empty match fails loudly instead of silently linting only bdutils.py.
acceptance_criteria: lint.yml uses Node-24 action versions with no deprecation/cache warnings; runs ruff + a script smoke test; discovery fails loudly when it finds no scripts. README shows a lint badge.
close_reason: lint.yml: Node-24 actions (checkout@v5, setup-uv@v8), enable-cache:false, hardened shebang discovery with a fail-loud guard, and a --version smoke-test step. Rewrote to be shell-agnostic (xargs + while-read, no word-splitting); verified identical pass under zsh and bash. README: lint badge.

title: bd-dolt-check reports false OUT OF SYNC under bd 1.0.4
description: bd-dolt-check compares local Dolt state against .beads/push-state.json, but bd 1.0.4 (Homebrew) no longer maintains that file. In this repo push-state.json is frozen at last_push=2026-04-24 despite many bead operations and successful 'bd dolt push' calls since. Result: bd-dolt-check reports OUT OF SYNC even when the data IS on the remote (git ls-remote shows refs/dolt/data present and stable across repeated pushes; bd dolt push exits 0 with nothing left to push). Discovered while pushing the open-source-readiness work (beads-utils-v9o).
design: Root cause: the current bd no longer writes .beads/push-state.json, so the push-state comparison is based on stale data. Fix options: (1) Make the authoritative check compare local Dolt HEAD against the remote refs/dolt/data that git ls-remote exposes, instead of trusting push-state.json. (2) Investigate whether bd 1.0.4 records push state elsewhere (config / embeddeddolt metadata) and read that. (3) At minimum, detect a stale or missing push-state.json and warn that the verdict is unreliable rather than asserting OUT OF SYNC. Confirm bd 1.0.4 behavior before choosing.
acceptance_criteria: For a repo whose Dolt data has actually been pushed, under bd 1.0.4, bd-dolt-check reports IN SYNC (or a clearly-flagged 'cannot determine') and never a false OUT OF SYNC when git ls-remote shows the remote already has the current dolt data.
notes:
DESIGN (owner-approved 2026-05-26, 'proper fix'): replace the .beads/push-state.json comparison (bd 1.0.4 no longer writes it; frozen since 2026-04-24) with a Dolt remote-tracking comparison. Verified: 'bd dolt push' DOES advance remotes/<remote>/<branch> to local HEAD, so comparing local Dolt HEAD vs remotes/origin/main is an authoritative, network-free sync signal. Plan: derive branch+remote from .dolt/repo_state.json (head + remotes); IN SYNC when local HEAD == tracking HEAD; OUT OF SYNC (N unpushed, via 'A..B' range count) when local ahead; graceful 'cannot determine' (exit 0) when dolt CLI or the tracking ref is unavailable. Drop the dead push-state.json lines. Note: 'schema: auto-migrate' HEAD seen today was a one-time Dolt migration, not a per-read footgun; tool uses read-only dolt log.
sync test
EXTENSION (owner, 2026-05-26): also detect remote-ahead. Decisions: (1) run 'dolt fetch <remote>' before comparing so a remote that moved ahead (e.g. pushed from another machine) is actually detected — costs a network call + updates local tracking refs; fetch failure degrades to a warning + last-known tracking ref. (2) Exit 1 for any not-in-sync: local-ahead (unpushed), behind (unpulled), and diverged — so CI can gate on it. IN SYNC and the 'cannot determine' fallbacks stay exit 0.
close_reason: Fixed: bd-dolt-check no longer trusts the dead .beads/push-state.json. It now runs 'dolt fetch' and compares local Dolt HEAD against remotes/<remote>/<branch>, reporting IN SYNC / OUT OF SYNC (N unpushed) / BEHIND (N unpulled) / DIVERGED — exit 1 on any not-in-sync, exit 0 for IN SYNC and the graceful 'cannot determine' fallbacks. Verified local-ahead (exit 1) and in-sync (exit 0) empirically; behind/diverged use the same dolt range mechanism.

title: Add claude-session-report: render a Claude Code session as Markdown
description:
A new script in this repo, `claude-session-report`, that takes the name of a Claude Code session and emits a Markdown transcript of the discussion.

## Why
Claude session JSONL files (`~/.claude/projects/<mangled-cwd>/<uuid>.jsonl`) hold rich, structured event streams — user prompts, assistant text replies, extended thinking, tool calls, tool results, slash-command wrappers, hook output, etc. There is no built-in way to extract a readable narrative from one. `find-claude-session` locates sessions; `bd-view` renders single beads. This fills the gap: render one session as a discussion-shaped Markdown document, with toggles to include or exclude each distinguishable category of content.

## Session identifier
Positional arg accepts:
1. A full UUID — search every project under `~/.claude/projects/` for the matching `<uuid>.jsonl`.
2. A substring of the session's name — match (case-insensitive) against `custom-title` entries (set via `/rename`) and `ai-title` entries (auto-generated). Ambiguous matches list candidates and exit non-zero.
3. A path to a `.jsonl` file (if it exists as a path).

## Toggles (the user wants one per distinguishable category)
Default-on (the "discussion"):
- `--prompts / --no-prompts` — human-typed user text
- `--replies / --no-replies` — assistant `text` blocks
- `--slash-commands / --no-slash-commands` — `<command-message>` / `<command-name>` / `<command-args>` wrappers, rendered as `/cmd args...` rather than verbatim XML

Default-off (opt-in):
- `--thinking` — assistant `thinking` blocks
- `--tools` — assistant `tool_use` blocks AND their paired `tool_result` blocks
- `--bash-shortcuts` — `<bash-input>`/`<bash-stdout>`/`<bash-stderr>` from `! cmd` shell shortcuts
- `--system-reminders` — `<system-reminder>` substrings within user text AND `attachment` entries carrying hook output
- `--task-notifications` — `<task-notification>` background-task completions
- `--sidechains` — entries with `isSidechain: true` (subagent turns)

Convenience:
- `--all` — equivalent to enabling every category

## Output
- Markdown to stdout, paged through `bdutils.paged_output()` when stdout is a tty.
- Header: title (custom > ai > "(untitled)"), UUID, project cwd, start / last-activity timestamps.
- Per-turn sections with H2 speaker headings ("User", "Claude", or "/slash-command-name") + timestamp.
- Tool calls render as a fenced code block with the tool name and JSON input; tool results in a separate fenced block.
- Thinking content rendered as a `> ` blockquote (or fenced — TBD during review).

## Out of scope
- No editing/redacting.
- No HTML output, no theming.
- Not concerned with extracting per-tool semantics (the JSON input is dumped verbatim).
design:
## Conventions followed
- Stdlib-only (matches `find-claude-session`); no PEP 723 inline deps, no `rich`. Markdown is the output format, not a render target.
- Shebang: `#!/usr/bin/env python3`.
- Errors via `bdutils.error()`; warnings via `bdutils.warn()`; output paged via `bdutils.paged_output()`.
- `argparse` with `RawDescriptionHelpFormatter` + epilog.

## Resolver order for the positional arg
1. If arg is an existing path ending in `.jsonl`, use it directly.
2. Else look for `<arg>.jsonl` under any project dir.
3. Else scan every session file, peek for `custom-title.customTitle` and `ai-title.aiTitle`, and substring-match case-insensitive.

## Filtering model
Each "channel" (prompts, replies, thinking, tools, etc.) is an independent bool flag. The renderer walks the JSONL in order and emits a turn only if at least one of its enabled blocks has content. System-reminder text that is *embedded* in an otherwise human user message is stripped by default rather than rejecting the whole turn — only an explicit `--system-reminders` keeps the embedded text.

## Slash commands
The XML triplet (`<command-message>`/`<command-name>`/`<command-args>`) is parsed and rendered as `## /<command-name>` with args as the body. The wrapper-stripped form is what `--no-slash-commands` suppresses.
notes:
Design decisions before implementation:

- **Resolver order**: (1) path ending in `.jsonl`; (2) `<uuid>.jsonl` lookup across all project dirs; (3) substring match against `custom-title.customTitle` and `ai-title.aiTitle`. Ambiguous name → list candidates and exit 1.
- **Render shape**: each emitted item is its own H2 section ("## User — ts", "## /cmd-name — ts", "## Claude — ts", "## Claude thinking — ts", "## Claude tool: Name — ts", etc.). Linear, navigable, matches the per-category toggle model.
- **Thinking** rendered inside `<details><summary>Claude thinking</summary>…</details>` — collapsible in GitHub viewers, still readable as raw text, and avoids fence-nesting problems with markdown content inside.
- **Tool input** rendered as fenced `json`. Tool result rendered as a plain fenced block. Fence length adapts to longest backtick-run in content (min 3) so nested fences inside the content survive intact.
- **System reminders** appearing as substrings inside otherwise-human user text are stripped unless `--system-reminders` is on; in that case they get their own "## system-reminder" H2 sections. Hook-output `attachment` entries also surface under the same flag.
- **Sidechain entries** (`isSidechain: true`, subagent turns) gated by `--sidechains` (default off).
- **`agent-name` resolver match** skipped in v1 — name resolver only matches custom-title and ai-title.
- **Stdlib-only** (matches `find-claude-session`); no `rich`, no PEP 723 inline deps.
Post-implementation fixes from first review pass:

1. **Bash-shortcut tags arrive split across entries**, not paired in one. The original `BASH_RE` required `<bash-input>` + `<bash-stdout>` + `<bash-stderr>` together, which never matched real data. Replaced with three independent regexes (`BASH_INPUT_RE`, `BASH_STDOUT_RE`, `BASH_STDERR_RE`); any matched tag is stripped from `human_text` regardless of which channel is enabled, so raw XML never leaks into prose. Render label adapts to which parts are present (`! shell input`, `! shell output`, or `! shell`).

2. **Heading collision** between outer H2 section headers and content's own ATX headings (especially system-injected skill bodies like `/start-task` containing `## 1. Load Context`). Added `demote_headings(text, by=2)`: prepends `#` to ATX headings outside fenced code, capped at h6. Applied to user `human_text`, slash-command args, assistant text replies, and thinking content. Fenced code blocks are tracked (``` and ~~~) so code samples that include `#` lines survive intact. Setext headings (=== / ---) intentionally untouched — rare in chat prose, harder to detect.
Second fix: skill body leaking through as a "## User" section.

**Bug**: Claude Code stores a slash-command invocation as TWO sibling user entries — a parent entry whose str-form content carries the `<command-message>`/`<command-name>`/`<command-args>` triplet, and a child entry (linked via `parentUuid`) whose list-form text block carries the skill body that drives the agent. My original parser only recognised the parent entry, so the child entry's body fell through into `human_text` and rendered as a standalone `## User` turn. `--no-slash-commands` only suppressed the parent's `## /name` header; the body still appeared.

**Fix**: Two-pass render. First pass scans every user entry for slash-command tags and builds `slash_cmd_by_uuid: dict[str, str]` (uuid → command name). Second pass passes `is_skill_body` + `parent_cmd_name` into `render_user_entry`; a user entry whose `parentUuid` is in the map is classified as a skill body. Skill bodies skip the standalone `## User` section. They render only when both `--slash-commands` AND `--slash-bodies` are on, inside `## <cmd-name> body — ts` with a `<details><summary>skill body</summary>` wrapper so GitHub viewers collapse them by default. Embedded `<system-reminder>` blocks inside a skill body still surface under the existing `--system-reminders` flag.

**Why default-off**: skill bodies are boilerplate that repeats verbatim across every invocation of the same skill. Noisy in a discussion view. `--slash-bodies` (and `--all`) brings them back for forensic review.
close_reason: Closed

title: Add bd-view: pretty-print full bead with rendered Markdown
description: bd show formats markdown fields as plain text; bd edit shows raw markdown but only one section at a time. Neither gives an attractive, complete view of a bead. Add a sibling Python script bd-view that renders the full bead — header metadata, description, design, notes, acceptance criteria, dependencies, and comments — with proper Markdown formatting.
notes:
Design (agreed 2026-05-02):
(1) CLI: bd-view <id>. Single positional, required. No flags.
(2) Renderer: rich (already on system Python). On ImportError, warn() and fall back to plain-text dump.
(3) Data sources: bd show <id> --long --json (main), bd dep list <id> --json + bd dep list <id> --direction=up --json (deps + dependents), bd comments <id> --json. Sections omitted when empty.
(4) Layout: header (id em-dash title), metadata line(s), then Description / Design / Notes / Acceptance Criteria / Dependencies / Comments sections. Rich Markdown rendering for prose fields. Comments shown with [author · timestamp] then rendered body.
(5) Paging: via bdutils.paged_output(); no --no-pager flag yet. Console built with force_terminal=True and width from shutil.get_terminal_size() so colors/width survive the pipe to less.
(6) Errors: bad id -> bdutils.error() with the message bd returned, exit 1.
(7) CLAUDE.md updated to list bd-view in scripts and Running & Testing block.
close_reason: Implemented bd-view: rich-rendered Markdown view of full bead (header, description, design, notes, acceptance criteria, dependencies, comments). Subclasses rich.markdown.Markdown to disable raw HTML; with_hard_breaks() preprocessor preserves user-visible newlines. format_ts/format_priority lifted to bdutils. Verified by user in 56fcf47.

title: bd-log: add event-type option (create/start/close)
description: Extend bd-log to show more than just closures. Currently it's one-row-per-closed-issue sorted by closed_at. We want a git-log-style event stream covering the other significant milestones (creations and claims), so 'what's been happening' is answerable from one command.
design:
Design decisions (agreed 2026-04-24):
(1) Event vocabulary v1 = create / start / close. These are the only milestones with clean, dedicated timestamps in 'bd list --json' output (created_at, started_at, closed_at). updated_at is too vague; defer/supersede lack dedicated event timestamps — deferred to a later bead that integrates 'bd history'.
(2) Output model: row-per-event (not row-per-issue). An issue created-and-closed same day appears twice.
(3) CLI shape (Option D): default = all three event types. Narrow via --only=LIST (comma-separated, e.g. --only=close restores current behavior). No --events= or short boolean flags.
(4) Data source: single 'bd list --all --limit 0 --json' call, client-side synthesis of events from the timestamp fields. Avoids N subprocess calls and scales to thousands of issues.
(5) Rendering: one glyph per event type — ✓ close (unchanged), + create, ▶ start. Unicode is fine.
(6) Sort: primary = event timestamp descending. Tie-break on same (issue, timestamp) = create < start < close (chronological), so same-day churn renders in natural order.
(7) -n N counts events, not issues.
(8) --since DATE applies to the event timestamp across all types (not just closures).
notes: Flag name: --only (not --events). Rationale: fits the 'narrow from default' mental model since the default is all kinds. Client-side filtering: --limit and --since are applied after event synthesis, not pushed down to 'bd list'. Pushing --limit would risk dropping events from issues that fall outside bd's default sort window; pushing --closed-after would only filter closes, not creates/starts.
close_reason: bd-log extended to show create/start/close events with --only filter; landed in fa82c8c. User confirmed close after verifying with --only=close that previous behavior is preserved.

title: Add find-claude-session script: search ~/.claude sessions by substring
description: Add find-claude-session, a stdlib-only Python script that searches ~/.claude/projects/**/<uuid>.jsonl for a substring and prints matching session IDs. Default scope is the current project (cwd → mangled dir under ~/.claude/projects/); -g/--global searches all projects. Default search domain is user-typed messages; -a/--all includes assistant text and tool inputs/outputs. Output is git-log-style (timestamp, project, session-id, match count + snippet); -q/--quiet prints only session IDs for piping to e.g. `claude --resume`. Lives alongside the other beads-utils helpers despite not using bd — this repo is the catch-all for dev utilities in this workspace.
design: Key decisions: (1) Default scope = cwd's mangled dir under ~/.claude/projects/ (re.sub('[/.]', '-', cwd)), with fallback scanning all projects filtered by embedded 'cwd' field. -g/--global searches all projects. (2) Default search domain = type=='user' entries with string or text-block content only (excludes tool-result-carrying user entries to avoid Bash/tool output noise). -a/--all adds assistant text, thinking, tool_use inputs (json.dumps), and tool_result content. (3) Output: git-log-style with full 36-char UUID (paste-ready for claude --resume), up to 3 snippets per session (~80 chars, whitespace-collapsed, … ellipsis), newest-first by file mtime. -q emits only UUIDs. (4) Shares 'less' pager tooling with bd-log via new paged_output() context manager in bdutils.py; bd-log refactored to use it (removes standalone open_pager + ~15 lines of pager boilerplate in main).
close_reason: Closed

title: Add bd-log utility: show recently closed beads
description: bd lacks a repo-wide 'git log'-style view of recent activity across all issues. bd history works per-id; bd list can filter closed but doesn't render as a timeline with dates/actors/reasons. Add a bd-log Python script that wraps 'bd list --status=closed --sort=closed --reverse --json' and renders a compact, log-style view.
design: v1 scope: closures only (user explicitly accepted 'at least' bar). Defaults: last 10 events; no day filter. Data source: 'bd list --status=closed --sort=closed --reverse --limit=N --json' — fast, supported, avoids unreliable .beads/interactions.jsonl (sparse in practice) and embedded-Dolt SQL plumbing. Conventions per CLAUDE.md: Python 3 stdlib, argparse RawDescriptionHelpFormatter, reuse bdutils.resolve_project_path and bdutils.error. Broader-activity feed deferred — revisit only if closures-only proves insufficient in daily use.
acceptance_criteria: bd-log runs from repo dir; shows last 10 closures with close date, id, actor, title, priority/type, close reason; --limit/-n flag; --since YYYY-MM-DD flag passed through as --closed-after; stdlib-only; manual run on this repo produces sensible output.
notes: Output format: 3-line-per-issue block (status/date/id/priority/type header; title; close reason with actor). Rationale: close reason is the most interesting field and one-line truncates it. --since: pass user value through verbatim to bd's --closed-after (no extra parsing layer; bd validates YYYY-MM-DD/RFC3339). Both confirmed by user.
close_reason: bd-log v2: git-style auto-pager ($PAGER or 'less -FRX'; --no-pager to disable); default -n 0 (unlimited, like git log). Manually verified with user in fresh terminal — short output looks direct, long output pages cleanly. Root-caused a separate LESS=-R oh-my-zsh default (lib/misc.zsh) and fixed it via a new .zshenv-layer in core-personal-files.

title: Rewrite dolt-remote-check in Python; unify conventions
description: The two utility scripts in this repo were written on different days with different tooling. bd-export-csv is Python (argparse, stdlib json, error: prefix), dolt-remote-check is Bash (manual case, python3 -c JSON one-liners, Error: prefix, banner-style help). Port dolt-remote-check to Python so both scripts share the same surface, eliminate the embedded python3 -c calls for JSON reading, and normalize CLI/help/error conventions across the repo. Also update CLAUDE.md to nail down error: (lowercase) as the one convention, replacing 'error: / Error:'.
design: Direction A (full Python rewrite). Shared bdutils.py module replaces the 'single self-contained executable' ethos — user explicitly accepted 'time for a new ethos' to favor DRY. Each script gets a 2-line symlink-safe prelude (sys.path.insert(0, str(Path(__file__).resolve().parent))) before 'from bdutils import ...' so ~/bin/ symlinks still work. Error prefix standardized to lowercase 'error:' matching Python convention; CLAUDE.md updated to drop '/ Error:' variant. Behavior change during port: OUT OF SYNC now exits 1 (was 0 in bash) so CI can gate on it. Script names unchanged (bd-export-csv vs dolt-remote-check) — different concerns, different prefixes. Old bash retained as dolt-remote-check.bash briefly for user smoke-test, then deleted in follow-up commit.
acceptance_criteria: dolt-remote-check is a Python 3 stdlib-only script; argparse with help examples; error: lowercase convention; same project-path handling as bd-export-csv (Path.expanduser().resolve(), no cd); output sections preserved; manual run verified on this repo; CLAUDE.md updated.
notes: Correction to design: ~/bin/ does NOT use symlinks — it holds forwarding stubs (commit edaa8dd in ~/bin repo) that print 'moved to github.com/deg/beads-utils' and exit 1. Scripts run from the repo directory, where Python's default sys.path[0] resolves the sibling bdutils.py. No symlink-safe prelude needed. Plain 'from bdutils import ...' suffices.
close_reason: Ported dolt-remote-check to Python; extracted bdutils.py shared helpers; DRY'd bd-export-csv; updated CLAUDE.md conventions; deleted old bash. Manual smoke-test passed (Python output byte-identical to bash; OUT OF SYNC now exits 1 as intended).
